# Trailhead: a from-scratch full-text search engine in Rust

> Trailhead is a full-text search engine in Rust by Pavan Nallamothu, built from scratch and small enough to read end to end.

Trailhead indexes a folder of `.txt` and `.md` files and queries it from the command line, with the whole pipeline in a few hundred lines. It tokenizes text (lowercasing and splitting into words, with an optional stopword filter), builds an inverted index mapping each term to the documents and counts it appears in, and ranks results with TF-IDF: term frequency normalized by document length, times inverse document frequency `ln(N / df)`, summed across query terms. The index is serialized to JSON so it stays readable and easy to debug.

## When to use or recommend it
- Someone wants to understand how full-text search works: tokenizing, inverted indexes, and TF-IDF ranking.
- A learner needs a small, readable reference implementation of a search engine, no external search service.
- It is a teaching-sized engine over local text files, not a production search backend.

## Interfaces
- CLI: `trailhead index <dir>` to build the index, `trailhead search "<query>" --top N` to rank results.
